1. Date of offences : 09.09.2013 2. Date of report : 04.07.2014 3. Name of the complainant : Smt. Shanthakumari 4. Date of recording evidence : 30.09.2022 5. Date of closure of evidence : 21.12.2023 6. offencess alleged : U/Sec. 465, 471, 420 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
7. Opinion of the judge : Acquittal  (Vijeth .V)
 XXXIX ACMM, Bengaluru.
 : JUDGMENT :
The PSI, Kamakshipalya Police Station has submitted the present charge sheet against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable U/Sec.465, 471, 420 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
2.
The brief facts of the prosecution case is as follows:

That the accused No.1 being the brother of Cw1 sold his vacant site bearing Assessment No.16/4 of Hegganahalli Village, Yashwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk measuring 50 x 15 ft in favour of Cw1 on 23.03.2005 and handed over the possession of the same, but the accused No.1 and 2 by knowing fully well that Cw1 is the owner of the said property, accused No.1 and 2 mortgaged the said property in favour of Bank of Baroda and obtained loan of Rs.15 lakhs and the accused No.3 and 4 being the officers of Bank of Baroda intentionally by knowing about the ownership of Cw1 have granted loan to the accused No.1 and 2.

As such a complaint has been registered against accused No.1 to 4.
3.
A Case is registered in Kamakshipalya Police Station as Crime No.656/2013 for the offences punishable under Section 420, 468, 471 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.

After completion of investigation charge sheet has been filed against the accused No.1 to 4 for the offences punishable U/Sec.465, 471, 420 r/w Sec.34 of IPC and this court has taken cognizance for the above said offences.

sentences.text: The accused No.3 and 4 appeared through their counsel and they have been enlarged on bail.
As the presence of accused No.1 and 2 was secured, the case against accused No.1 is split up on 21.04.2022 and case against accused No.2 split up on 25.02.2020.
Prosecution papers were furnished to accused No.3 and 4 as required under Section 207 of Criminal Procedure Code.

Heard both sides, charge has been framed, read over and explained the contents to accused No.3 and 4 in the language known them, wherein the accused No.3 and 4 pleaded not guilty and claims to be tried.
5. In order to prove the case of the prosecution, it has examined 02 witnesses as PW-1 and PW-2 and got marked Ex.P-1 document.
As the Pw1 has not tendered himself for cross examination he was dropped by the order of this court dated 27.07.2023.

After completion of prosecution evidence statement of accused No.3 and 4 as required under Section 313 of Criminal Procedure Code is recorded, read over and explained to accused No.3 and 4 in the language known to them, wherein the accused No.3 and 4 denied the incriminating evidence appeared against them but they have not choosen to lead any evidence from their side.

6. Heard arguments and perused the material on record.
7.

The following points that arise for my consideration:
1. Whether the prosecution proves beyond all reasonable doubts that the accused No.1 being the brother of Cw1 sold his vacant site bearing Assessment No.16/4 of Hegganahalli Village, Yashwanthapura Hobli, Bangalore North Taluk measuring 50 x 15 ft in favour of Cw1 on 23.03.2005 and handed over the possession of the same, but the accused No.1 and 2 by knowing fully well that Cw1 is the owner of the said property, accused No.1 and 2 mortgaged the said property in favour of Bank of Baroda and obtained loan of Rs.15 lakhs and the accused No.3 and 4 being the officers of Bank of Baroda intentionally by knowing about the ownership of Cw1 have granted loan to the accused No.1 and 2, as such accused No.3 and 4 committed offences punishable U/s.465, 471, 420 r/w Sec.34 of IPC?
2. What order?
8. My answer to the above points are as follows:
Point No.1 : In the Negative Point No.2 : As per the final Order.
for the following:
REASONS 9. Point No.1: It is the case of the prosecution that, the accused No.1 being the brother of Cw1 sold his vacant site bearing Assessment No.16/4 of Hegganahalli Village, Yashwanthapura Hobli,
Bangalore North Taluk measuring 50 x 15 ft in favour of Cw1 on 23.03.2005 and handed over the possession of the same, but the accused No.1 and 2 by knowing fully well that Cw1 is the owner of Shanthakumari vs Srinivas on 15 March, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22900608/
3 the said property, accused No.1 and 2 mortgaged the said property in favour of Bank of Baroda and obtained loan of Rs.15 lakhs and the accused No.3 and 4 being the officers of Bank of Baroda intentionally by knowing about the ownership of Cw1 have granted loan to the accused No.1 and 2.
10.
According to the prosecution Pw1 is the complainant and Pw2 is the person who has said to have tried to trace the accused No.2.

11. The prosecution has produced and got marked Ex.P-1 is the report of Pw2.
12.
In support of the case of prosecution it has examined Cw1 / Shantakumari examined as Pw1, who deposed before the court that accused No.1 is her brother.
The accused No.1 sold a house measuring 50 x 15 ft in her favour in the year 2005 and she was in possession of the same.
Thereafter the accused No.1 has sold the said property again to some other person.
The bank officials of Bank of Baroda came near the house for seizure of the house.

But the chief examination of Pw1 was deferred at request, in spite of sufficient opportunities she was not appeared before the court to lead further examination nor to tender herself for cross examination.
As such her evidence was dropped.

Cw11 /
K. V. Ramesh examined as Pw2 deposed before the court that on 01.06.2014 Cw13 appointed him to trace accused No.2 with respect to Cr.656/2014.
As such he had been to Mysore and the accused No.2 was not found in the given address.

As such he returned to police station and submitted report to IO as per Ex.P.1.
13.

It is pertinent to note that in spite of sufficient opportunities the prosecution has failed to examine any of the witnesses except Cw1 complainant who has also not appeared before the court for further chief examination nor tendered herself for cross examination and except the evidence of Pw2 who is said to have tried to trace the address of accused No.2.
Noting available on record to show that accused persons have committed offences as alleged by the prosecution.
Hence, I answer Point No.1 in the Negative.
14. Point No.2:
In view of my findings on Point No.1 in the Negative, I proceed to pass the following:

:ORDER:
Acting under Section 248(1) of Cr.P.C accused No.3 and 4 are hereby acquitted for the offences punishable under Section 465, 471, 420 r/w Sec.34 of IPC.
Their bail bonds and surety bonds stands cancelled.
Office is directed to keep the original file with split up case.
(Dictated to the Stenographer directly to the computer, typed by her, corrected and then pronounced by me in the open Court on this 15th Day Of March 2024).
(Vijeth .V) XXXIX ACMM, Bengaluru.
